        odd = all(x % 2 == 1 for x in xs)
        r10 = len(set(x % 10 for x in xs)) == 1 and len(xs) > 1

    n = s.map(lambda u: info[u][0]).to_numpy()
    lo = s.map(lambda u: info[u][1]).to_numpy()
    hi = s.map(lambda u: info[u][2]).to_numpy()
    kmax = s.map(lambda u: info[u][3]).to_numpy()
    odd = s.map(lambda u: info[u][4]).to_numpy().astype(bool)
    r10 = s.map(lambda u: info[u][5]).to_numpy().astype(bool)

"    m = ruled & (n > 1) & member & (dist > 0)\n    if m.sum() < 3:\n        return 0.0\n    d = dist[m] / 10.0\n    yy = y[m]\n    v = np.var(d)\n    return float(np.mean((d - d.mean()) * (yy - yy.mean())) / v) if v > 0 else 0.0"),
"parity_only_far_member_yes": ("Yes-rate for rule members more than 20 from the examples' span, in multi-example sets whose only shared rule is even (k=2) or odd; observed < null means people generalise weak parity rules to far numbers less than the model.",
"    m = (n > 1) & ((kmax == 2) | (odd & (kmax == 0))) & member & (dist > 20)\n    return rate(m)"),
"single_example_rule_partner_vs_neighbour": ("For single-example sets, yes-rate for targets within 3 of the example minus yes-rate for targets 4-30 away sharing its last digit; observed > null means people rely on numeric proximity more (and digit/rule partners less) than the model.",
"    m = (n == 1)\n    near = m & (dist > 0) & (dist <= 3)\n    part = m & (dist >= 4) & (dist <= 30) & (t % 10 == last)\n    return rate(near) - rate(part)"),
"unmodelled_residue_class_contrast": ("For multi-example sets whose examples all share a last digit that is not 0 (e.g. 7,17,37), yes-rate for targets sharing that last digit minus other targets; observed > null means people pick up same-last-digit concepts more strongly than the model.",
"    m = r10 & (last != 0)\n    return rate(m & (t % 10 == last) & (dist == 0) | m & (t % 10 == last) & (dist > 0)) - rate(m & (t % 10 != last))"),

"    m = (~ruled) & (n > 1)\n    return rate(m & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 5)) - rate(m & inhull)"),
"wide_pair_inhull_nonmember_yes": ("Yes-rate for in-span targets that are not rule members in two-example sets spanning more than 40; observed > null means people treat widely spaced pairs as covering the range between them more than the model.",
"    m = (n == 2) & (span > 40) & inhull & (~member)\n    return rate(m)"),
}

I've written all 8 test statistics to `iter_1/critique/test_stats/`. Each ran once on the observed responses and returned a finite number in about 0.013 s, well under the 0.3 s budget. None of the files imports anything; they use only the `np`, `pd` and `math` already in scope. The forbidden `import pandas` is what disqualified every statistic in the first attempt. I didn't run the posterior-predictive harness, so there are no p-values yet. I also didn't check how many trials fall into each subset, so a few statistics may rest on small subsets.

Each file works out the set's properties itself. That includes the span of the examples, the largest k (2–10) that all examples are multiples of, whether they are all odd, and how far the target falls outside the span. The statistics are:

| Statistic | What it measures | Observed value |
|---|---|---|
| `far_nonmember_small_minus_large` | Sets with no shared multiple or odd rule: yes-rate for targets more than 10 below the span minus more than 10 above it | −0.062 |
| `narrow_rule_inhull_nonmember_span_contrast` | Rule sets: yes-rate for rule non-members inside the span, wide spans (over 40) minus narrow spans | −0.305 |
| `narrow_rule_outside_distance_slope` | Rule sets: slope of yes-rate against distance (per 10 units) for rule members outside the span | −0.004 |
| `parity_only_far_member_yes` | Sets whose only shared rule is even or odd: yes-rate for members more than 20 outside the span | 0.333 |
| `single_example_rule_partner_vs_neighbour` | One-example sets: yes-rate within ±3 of the example minus targets 4–30 away that share its last digit | 0.035 |
| `unmodelled_residue_class_contrast` | Sets whose examples share a non-zero last digit (e.g. 7, 17, 37): yes-rate for targets with that last digit minus the rest | 0.529 |
| `unruled_set_near_edge_extension` | Sets with no shared rule: yes-rate 1–5 outside the span minus inside it | 0.045 |
| `wide_pair_inhull_nonmember_yes` | Two-example sets spanning more than 40: yes-rate for in-span targets that aren't rule members | 0.370 |

Each file's `# description:` line says which direction of discrepancy means what, so the next round can read the results directly.
